annotations.title: Mark up my open Vela chart

description: Marks up the chart the signed-in member has open right now in Vela the way a professional discretionary trader would, from the chart's own candles: fair value gaps, buyside and sellside liquidity and equal highs and lows, market structure (BOS and MSS), order blocks and breakers, the dealing range with premium, discount and OTE, opening gaps, ICT killzones and macros, key levels (previous day and week high and low, midnight open, session highs and lows), support and resistance, trendlines, chart patterns, and a range with extensions. You name the concepts and Vela finds the exact prices and times itself, so never pass prices you made up; the member watches each one being drawn, as real, labelled drawings in Vela's house style. Use it whenever the member asks to mark up, annotate or analyse their chart, or to be shown where something is on it; it works on every market Vela charts (stocks, futures, forex, crypto), and a new markup of a concept replaces your earlier one. Give each concept an explain and the member is walked through the markup on their chart, your words in a bubble on each part: the way to teach a setup. Returns what was found, each with its time and state; with exact prices for a crypto chart fed by an exchange (Binance, Binance.US, Coinbase, Hyperliquid), and without prices for any other market, where the drawings still sit at their exact levels for the member to read. For drawings at prices you choose yourself (a scenario, a target, a plan) use vela_draw_on_chart. With the member's Vela tab on screen it happens in front of them within seconds. When it is not (they are in another tab), the change is queued and applied the moment they look at Vela again, within 10 minutes: the result then says queued, so tell them to open Vela. Requires signing in with a LuxAlgo account (OAuth).

concepts.description: What to mark up, up to six concepts in one go.

concept.description: What to find and draw: fair_value_gaps; liquidity (buyside and sellside, equal highs and lows, sweeps); market_structure (BOS and MSS); order_blocks (and breakers); dealing_range (the range split at equilibrium into premium and discount); opening_gaps (NWOG, NDOG); killzones and macros (ICT session windows, New York time); key_levels (previous day and week high and low, midnight open, session highs and lows); support_resistance; trendlines; pattern (channel, wedge, triangle); range (a range high and low with extensions).

count.description: How many to draw, nearest to price first.

days.description: killzones, macros: days back to draw (0 is today only).

explain.description: One or two plain sentences on what this part is and why it matters here. With it, the member is walked through the parts on their chart, a bubble on each in turn with Next and Exit: use it whenever you are teaching or presenting an analysis.

gap_kind.description: opening_gaps: NWOG (week, the default), NDOG (day) or both.

high.description: dealing_range, range: a range high the member named.

include_mitigated.description: fair_value_gaps: also show the last filled gaps.

include_swept.description: liquidity: show recently swept levels (default true).

inversions.description: fair_value_gaps: mark gaps closed through as inversion FVGs.

leg.description: dealing_range: the leg's direction, needed only when a named high or low did not trade on the loaded bars.

levels.description: key_levels: which levels (default previous-day and midnight-open).

low.description: dealing_range, range: a range low the member named.

mitigation.description: fair_value_gaps: filled once price trades through the far edge (full, the default) or reaches the 50% CE.

only.description: killzones, macros: only these windows by name, e.g. ["NY AM"].

strength.description: Swing strength in bars per side (the default suits the timeframe).

windows.description: killzones, macros: your own New York windows, e.g. [{"name":"Macro","start":"09:50","end":"10:10"}].

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

replace.description: Remove the earlier markup of the same concepts first (default true), so a redraw never stacks.

slot.description: One chart of a multi-chart layout, by position (0 is the top-left, in reading order). Leave it out for the chart the member is working on.
